---
title: "Lab · Greeting Capsule (Steps 4–5)"
---

The lab for this lesson is the shared
[**Greeting Capsule**](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/) lab —
the same lab [Module 2](../01-define-a-capsule/lab.qmd) uses, picked
up at the implementation and testing steps. It lives at the
repository root so Module 4 can reuse the same solution tree.

For Module 3 ("Implement and test a capsule") only **Steps 4–5** of
the walkthrough are in scope: implement the capability in a stdlib
Python function behind the contract, then run the two test modules
under `solution/tests/`. Steps 1–3 (fetch, author, validate the
capsule document) belong to Module 2; Steps 6–7 (compose a Pico,
hand-resolve the capability) belong to Module 4.

## What this lab covers for Module 3

- [Step 4 — Implement the capability](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html#step-4-implement-the-capability)
  creates `solution/greeting.py`: a single Python stdlib function
  behind the capsule's declared `spec.inputs`/`spec.outputs`, with a
  structured `MissingRequiredInput` error on a missing required input.
  See [`solution/greeting.py`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/solution/greeting.py)
  for the reference implementation (44 lines, no non-stdlib imports).
- [Step 5 — Run the tests](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html#step-5-run-the-tests)
  runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s solution/tests` and expects
  `Ran 8 tests in 0.001s` / `OK`. The two test modules —
  [`test_greeting.py`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/solution/tests/test_greeting.py)
  (unit) and
  [`test_contract.py`](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/solution/tests/test_contract.py)
  (contract, derived from `solution/capsule.yaml`) — cover the two
  failure modes the [lesson](index.qmd#unit-tests-vs-contract-tests)
  separates.

::: {.callout-important title="Course-local call convention"}
The function-call shape (`greeting(inputs: dict) -> dict`) used in
Steps 4–5 is a **course-local teaching harness**. The implementation
convention for capsules belongs to `open-engineering-capsule/source`,
which has published none yet
([`memo24.md`](../../../../memo24.md) §2.1 as updated by observation
at upstream commit `bf071c2c1b57`). When that convention is
published, the Academy will consume it; this lab will not fork or
shadow it ([`memo23.md`](../../../../memo23.md) §3.2,
[`memo26.md`](../../../../memo26.md) §5).
:::

## What you will produce

By the end of Step 5 you will have:

- `labs/greeting-capsule/solution/greeting.py` — a stdlib Python
  function behind the capsule contract, with a named exception on a
  missing required input;
- a passing run of `python3 -m unittest discover -s solution/tests`
  showing both the unit tests (`test_greeting.py`) and the contract
  tests (`test_contract.py`, derived from `solution/capsule.yaml`)
  succeed.

That evidence satisfies memo23 §4 Module 3 ("an independently
testable implementation, repeatable tests, and documented dependency
requirements") at the capsule level; Module 4 adds the composition
tier.

## What this lab does *not* do (in Module 3)

- It does **not** author or revalidate the capsule document. Steps
  1–3 belong to [Module 2](../01-define-a-capsule/lab.qmd).
- It does **not** compose a Pico or hand-resolve the capability.
  Steps 6–7 belong to Module 4 ("Compose a Pico").
- It does **not** introduce a database, broker, AI library, bot
  platform, or Kubernetes. The implementation and both test modules
  run on Python 3.8+ and `pyyaml` alone.
- It does **not** publish a reference implementation convention; the
  function-call harness is a teaching device until the implementation
  org publishes one (see the callout above).
